issues.legal_issue: A permanent allowance paid in lieu of former proprietary rights does not cease merely because the estates in which the recipient formerly held proprietary interests vest in the State.
material_facts: The recipient had long received a permanent allowance in lieu of proprietary rights in land formerly held by him.
The estates in which he held proprietary interests vested in the State after a vesting notification.
The State stopped paying the allowance on the ground that it had vested along with the estates.
Cess had been deducted from the allowance, but the Court held that this did not establish that the allowance was an interest in the estates.
issues.conclusion: The allowance was not an interest in the estates that vested and did not cease on their vesting; the State remained obliged to pay it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 4(a) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, vesting transferred the estate and the interests in it, but did not extinguish a separate permanent monetary allowance granted in lieu of former proprietary rights. The Court relied on State of Uttar Pradesh v. Kunwar Sri Trivikram Narain Singh, which held that an allowance paid for abandonment of rights in estates was not itself an interest in land. It also considered the historical character of permanent malikana as a compensatory, pensionary grant.

predicates.appeal_from_order_enforcing_allowance_pa: The matter is an appeal from an order requiring payment of an allowance.
predicates.estates_vested_in_state: The estates in which the recipient held proprietary interests passed to the State under a vesting process.
predicates.permanent_allowance_paid_for_former_prop: The recipient received a permanent allowance in consideration of proprietary rights in land that had been lost.
predicates.allowance_is_separate_from_vested_estate: The allowance was not an interest in, income from, or charge on the estates that vested.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns payment of an allowance after estates vest, and the allowance is a separate permanent grant for former proprietary rights, the allowance survives the vesting.

issues.legal_issue: A recipient who is not an intermediary of the estates for which a permanent allowance is paid has no intermediary interest in those estates that vests in the State or gives rise to intermediary compensation.
material_facts: The State contended that the allowance related to other estates and that the recipient was an intermediary of temporarily settled estates.
Documents showed that persons other than the recipient were proprietors of the estates for which the allowance was payable, and those estates had vested in the State.
The recipient was not a proprietor, tenure-holder, or intermediary of those estates.
The allowance was not rent or income derived from those estates and was not an encumbrance on them.
issues.conclusion: The recipient's right to the allowance was not an intermediary interest that vested in the State, and he was not entitled to compensation for its transfer under section 24A.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(jj), 2(jjj), and 2A of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950 define an intermediary and an intermediary interest by reference to a person's interest in an estate or tenure; section 24A provides compensation for transfer of an intermediary's interest in a temporarily settled estate. Because the recipient held no such interest, the allowance was not subject to vesting as an intermediary interest and did not qualify for compensation under section 24A. The Court referred to Bhoalee Singh v. Mst. Neemoo Behoo and Syed Shah Najamuddin Hyder v. Syed Zahid Hossein for the proposition that malikana is not rent; it also referred to Maharaja P. S. Bahadur v. State of Bihar and Mahendra Narayan Roy Chowdhuri v. Abdul Gafur Choudhry. It distinguished Herranund Shoo v. Mst. Ozeerun, Gobinda Chunder Roy Choudhuri v. Ram Chunder Chowdhury, Hurmuzi Begum v. Hirday Narayan, and Jaggo Bai v. Utsava Lal, which concerned different statutory or procedural contexts.

rule.if: appeal_from_order_enforcing_allowance_payment and allowance_relates_to_vested_estates and recipient_is_not_intermediary_of_those_estates and allowance_is_not_rent_or_income_from_estates and allowance_is_not_encumbrance_on_estates

predicates.appeal_from_order_enforcing_allowance_pa: The matter is an appeal from an order requiring payment of an allowance.
predicates.allowance_relates_to_vested_estates: The allowance is paid in connection with estates that have passed to the State.
predicates.recipient_is_not_intermediary_of_those_e: The recipient does not hold an ownership, tenure, or other intermediary interest in the estates for which the allowance is paid.
predicates.allowance_is_not_rent_or_income_from_est: The allowance is not rent or income derived from the estates.
predicates.allowance_is_not_encumbrance_on_estates: The allowance does not burden the estates as an encumbrance.

issues.definition: When an allowance relates to estates that vest but its recipient has no intermediary interest in them and it is neither their income nor an encumbrance on them, the allowance survives without intermediary compensation.
